subject: AtlasMobile: sudden spike in 429/503s — suspected burst/quota policy issue
messages:
From: Sophie Martin <sophie@atlasmobile.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: AtlasMobile: spike in 429/503s since 09:00 PDT

Hi Priyom / Neha,

We started seeing a large spike in 429 and occasional 503 responses from Redwood around 09:00 PDT this morning. Impact is across our mobile auth and search endpoints — we’re seeing ~18% error rate on user-facing requests and ~40% increased latency on successful requests. Our telemetry shows failed requests return a 429 with "burst_quota_exceeded" in the body (we've attached a short excerpt).

This is customer-impacting (downtime on some login flows). We have a large traffic surge this morning but nothing out of ordinary for event days; this started abruptly at 09:00. Can you confirm whether any quota/burst policy changes or routing adjustments were applied?

Attachments: [atlas_error_log_excerpt.txt — 28KB]

Sophie Martin
Platform Ops
AtlasMobile
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sophie Martin <sophie@atlasmobile.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Sep 2025 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AtlasMobile: spike in 429/503s since 09:00 PDT

Thanks for flagging, Sophie — we see the same signals on our side.

Neha / Karthik / Marissa: can the infra/serving teams triage? Initial symptom looks like aggressive token-bucket enforcement for AtlasMobile (429s with burst_quota_exceeded) that started when a routing policy was deployed this morning.

Immediate asks:
- Confirm whether a config change (burst_window, credits, or routing rules) hit production at ~09:00 PDT.
- If config change caused this, can we: 1) temporarily increase burst credits for AtlasMobile, and 2) route traffic to the fallback Dedicated pool while we patch the policy?

Sophie — we will treat this as a P1. I’ll update you with mitigation ETA in ~20–30 mins.

— Priyom
Head of Customer Escalations, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Sep 2025 09:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AtlasMobile: spike in 429/503s since 09:00 PDT

Quick triage notes (what I see in the runtime):
- At 08:59:56 PDT a routing policy push included an updated pacing profile for several Dedicated pools; the new profile reduced per-tenant burst_window from 300s to 60s for the "shared-high" pool.
- AtlasMobile's traffic was still pinned to their dedicated slot but relied on the older burst budget assumptions (longer window + credit refill). The new smaller window causes the token-bucket to exhaust faster under their morning burst, producing 429s with the "burst_quota_exceeded" tag.
- Some 503s are downstream from our fallback healthchecks failing while the pool was under heavy shedding; not primary.

Immediate mitigations in-flight:
1) Raised AtlasMobile burst credits on the affected pool (+2x for the next 30m) — already applied (monitoring).
2) Initiated a targeted routing shift to the secondary Dedicated pool for traffic from AtlasMobile (estimated gradual shift over 3–5 mins to avoid cache/KV warmup).
3) Opened OPS ticket: OPS-9472 (link in thread).

Next steps:
- Roll back the 08:59 policy change or adjust the burst_window to previous value (prefer rollback for safety).
- Postmortem to follow; recommend we include a guard in the deployment pipeline to block burst_window reductions for accounts with sustained high baseline QPS.

Attachments: [throttle_playbook_summary.pdf — 92KB]

Karthik
Senior Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Martin <sophie@atlasmobile.com>, Atlas Mobile Ops <ops@atlasmobile.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Sep 2025 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AtlasMobile: spike in 429/503s since 09:00 PDT

Sophie — short update and apology:

We identified a pacing/profile change deployed at ~08:59 that unintentionally reduced the burst_window for the pool serving AtlasMobile. That reduced the account's effective burst capacity and triggered the 429s you saw.

What we did:
- Immediately increased burst credits for AtlasMobile and diverted traffic to a secondary Dedicated pool (these are live now).
- Traffic and error rates are improving; monitoring shows error-rate down from ~18% to ~3% over the last 10 minutes.
- We are reverting the 08:59 change to restore previous burst_window within the hour and will validate at scale.

Customer remediation and asks:
- We will provide a formal incident timeline and postmortem by EOD tomorrow.
- As a gesture for the outage, we propose a one-month service credit. Please let us know if that is acceptable and provide any further impact details (user-facing metrics) so we can quantify the credit.

Again — deeply sorry for the disruption. We’ll follow up with the full remediation plan and the postmortem.

— Priyom
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Sep 2025 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Exec brief: AtlasMobile P1 (burst_window reduction caused production 429s)

Laura — brief summary and ask:

What happened:
- An infra routing/pacing change at 08:59 reduced burst_window for the shared-high Dedicated pool from 300s to 60s. AtlasMobile, which has sustained high baseline QPS, hit its token-bucket drain threshold and observed elevated 429s/503s from 09:00–09:40.

Impact:
- Customer-facing errors ~18% at peak for ~40 minutes; partial degradation to auth/search flows for end users. Customer reports increased support volume; incident is logged as P1.

Actions taken:
- Raised burst credits and routed traffic to secondary pool (mitigation succeeded; error rate down to ~1–3%).
- Rolling back the pacing change and adding a pipeline guard to prevent reductions to burst_window for high-QPS tenants.

Asks:
- Approval to issue a one-month credit to AtlasMobile (we offered already pending your sign-off).
- Exec-level note to Sales/GTM to coordinate customer communication and ensure retention risk is tracked.

I'll attach the postmortem draft once complete.

— Priyom
Head of Customer Escalations
Redwood Inference
